findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Observed buildup of soil residues in the soda nozzles. CORRECTED: PIC was notified, and relayed that establishment has a procedure for cleaning nozzles, and showed inspectors the sanitizing container, complete with a nozzle brush. Inspector and PIC discussed reminding staff to really scrub the nozzles so that they are clean to sight and touch. PIC had staff replace the used nozzles with clean nozzles during the inspection. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed several instances where food contact surfaces of single-service and single-use articles were stored upright without protection from contamination from above: dishes on top of counters, dishes on open wire racks, dishes inside of coolers. CORRECTED: PIC was informed and corrected each instance through inversion. Inspectors and PIC discussed better storage methods for open wire racks including placing plastic mats or other coverings on shelves. PIC also plans to educate staff on consistent storage methods of single-service and single-use articles. Ensure that food contact surfaces are protected through cover or inversion.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(C) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (C) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored as specified under (A) of this section and shall be kept in the original protective PACKAGE or stored by using other means that afford protection from contamination until used. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: 1ST REPEAT: Inspectors observed an accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezers and some reach-in freezers. PIC and Inspector discussed improved defrost procedures and increase cleaning frequency. Ensure that areas are smooth and easily cleanable, and are cleaned frequently.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed a staff person put on gloves without handwashing first. Education was carried out. Ensure that staff know to wash their hands before putting on gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.16(B) Hand Antiseptics. (B) If a hand antiseptic or a hand antiseptic solution used as a hand dip does not meet the criteria specified under Subparagraph (A)(2) of this section, use shall be: (1) Followed by thorough hand rinsing in clean water before hand contact with FOOD or by the use of gloves; or (2) Limited to situations that involve no direct contact with FOOD by the bare hands.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed improper storage order of raw meat, specifically steak stored above fish, in a cooler. The PIC was notified about the issue, and the steak was moved below the fish. Ensure that food is properly stored per storage order guidelines.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed buildup of soil residues in the soda nozzles. PIC was notified, and the nozzles were removed for cleaning and sanitizing, and also replaced some with newer clean nozzles. Ensure that all food-contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed the following items that need cleaning:
(1) The area between the grill and reach-in coolers in the Grill area was observed to have an accumulation of grease and soil residues.
(2) An accumulation of food debris and grease on surfaces near the fryer area.
(3) An accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezers and reach-in freezer.
Ensure that areas are smooth and easily cleanable, and are cleaned frequently.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee at the grill station used their barehand to turn off the faucet after hand washing. The employee was educated about the proper hand washing procedure when the action was observed. Ensure that employees always use a barrier to turn off the faucet to avoid re-contaminating clean hands.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment: Observed knives at the deli stored with the blade in the gap between the prep cooler and prep counter. The PIC and deli employees were informed that the knives could become contaminated stored inside the gap. The knives were moved into a new location during the inspection. Ensure that in-use utensils are stored in a location that is routinely cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The particle board holding utensils on the wall outside the main walk-in cooler and the wall by the prep cooler in the on-the-go room must be sealed (ex. painted). 

(2) The plastic cornering in the small dish washing room (near the tray line kitchen) by the entrance and the large dish washing room by the dish machine have fallen off the wall and must be replaced/repaired.

Ensure that all the above referenced are repaired/replaced/sealed to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the internal fans in the grill double door cooler have an accumulation of dust and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Observed there is a leak in the hand washing sink in the small dish washing room (near to the tray line kitchen). Ensure that the leak is repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 5-202.11(A) Approved System and Cleanable Fixtures. (A) A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be designed, constructed, and installed according to LAW.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Observed the following are not smooth, easily cleanable surfaces: 

(1) The particle board holding utensils on the wall outside the main walk-in cooler and the wall by the prep cooler in the on-the-go room must be sealed (ex. painted). 

(2) The plastic cornering in the small dish washing room by the entrance and the large dish washing room by the dish machine have fallen off the wall and must be replaced/repaired.

(3) The holes in the large dish washing room (near the triple sink) wall must be filled (ex. caulking).

(4) The caulking on the table behind the dish machine in the large dish washing room (attached to the rinsing table) is pulling away from the wall and must be re-sealed (ex. caulking). 

Ensure that all the above referenced are repaired/replaced/sealed to make smooth, easily cleanable surfaces by the next routine inspection. 

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed that various coffee machines throughout the facility (including, but not limited to, the customer self service area and the bakery kitchen) have an accumulation of soil on the under shelf that is in contact with the coffee pot top. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of soil residues. Ensure that the under shelf of the coffee machines are clean to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the gaskets of the stacked double cooler (to the right of the Pepsi cooler) in the tray line kitchen are in disrepair. The gaskets must be replaced/repaired by the next routine inspection to ensure that physical facilities are always maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed that a clean cutting board was stored behind the faucet at the catering double sink. The cutting board was removed from this position and staff was educated about proper storage of clean items. Ensure that food contact surfaces always remain clean to sight and touch. 

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following sinks need to be re-caulked: (1) The caulking at the bakery double sink is deteriorating and starting to mold; and (2) The caulking at the back triple sink in the dish area still being remodeled has almost completely peeled off. The PIC submitted a work order for caulking these areas during the inspection. Ensure they are re-caulked to be smooth, durable, and easily cleanable before the next routine inspection.   

6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the retail prep cooler top/action station were observed out of temperature (probed): chicken salad, 50F; egg salad, 49F; tuna salad, 49F; chicken, 53F; and ham, 46F. CORRECTED- Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Foods in the attached drawer coolers were all 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Foods were observed out of temperature in the action station prep cooler. Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded. Make the necessary repairs or adjustments to ensure that the cooler holds foods at 41F or below. Discussed options to maintain operations until the cooler is fully functional again (time as a control).
4-301.11: EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Cloths were observed on the floor under the front of the fryers, to soak up grease drips/spills. Discussed cloth use. If towels are needed to soak up spills, they should not remain in place for extended periods of time or overnight. Towels used for spills should be used then removed to be laundered. The towels observed during this inspection were removed. See that towels are removed after cleaning up spills. If needed, make repairs to the fryer or adjustments to employee procedures to prevent spills.
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Wet cardboard and slight soil accumulation observed under the Pepsi storage shelves and syrups. Clean floors.
2) Hood baffles at the Grill observed to be soiled. Clean baffles.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
Inspector observed several cans in dry storage which were damaged along either upper or lower seams. The cans had facility date labels attached indicating that they had been stocked in for service. The integrity of the seal on cans with dented seams cannot be guaranteed and increases the risk of botulism to patients/consumers. The cans were immediately discarded and the practice will be corrected with staff. Corrected on site. No follow-up required at this time. 

3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
Wiping cloths were observed in green detergent buckets. Wiping cloths must be stored in sanitizer between uses to prevent microbial growth and facilitate contact time with the sanitizer to kill bacteria. Buckets have been remade and wiping cloths have been placed in the sanitizer buckets as required. Work with staff to ensure that wiping cloths are stored properly at all times. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
In the dining area of the cafeteria, several personal drinks, a phone and lighter were observed near food/in coolers with facility food despite the presence of designated drink areas for employees. Ensure that staff are aware that personal items must be stored in designated areas at all times and may never be stored in direct contact with, above, or next to foods intended for service. Personal items were immediately removed. Corrected on site. No follow-up required. 

6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The caulking around the mop sink/utility drain and the caulking around the hand sink in the pots/pans cleaning area are observed to be deteriorating. Re-caulk these areas by the next routine inspection to ensure a smooth, easily cleanable surface. 

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Observed soda nozzles in the cafeteria to be soiled. The soda nozzles were pulled for cleaning during the inspection. Ensure soda nozzles are cleaned more frequently so they are clean to sight and touch.
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.
